candidate_relations.reason: Progressive cognitive and behavioral change is compatible with neurodegeneration but does not specify Lewy body disease or catatonia.
Mirtazapine timing alone cannot account for echopraxia, mitmachen, mutism, and staring.
Vitamin B12 was elevated at 1154.67 pmol/L rather than deficient.
A three-month decline with multiple specific catatonic signs is not adequately characterized as delirium.
Her prior depression does not explain new hallucinations, failure to recognize family, and motor catatonia at age 68.
Hallucinations and paranoid delusions are prominent manifestations but omit the cognitive decline and catatonic motor syndrome.
EEG showed only diffuse slowing and MRI lacked the diffusion-restriction pattern expected in CJD.
Rapid plasma reagin and cerebrospinal infectious evaluation were negative.
Normal TSH and unrevealing autoimmune cerebrospinal studies provide no support for Hashimoto encephalopathy.
Measured B12 was well above the normal range despite neuropsychiatric symptoms.
Failure to recognize family and progressive mental decline support dementia, but neither Lewy body subtype nor catatonia is captured.
Thyroid-stimulating hormone was normal and the extensive encephalopathy workup found no thyroid-mediated process.
MRI changes were judged chronic ischemia and there were no focal deficits or stepwise strokes to establish vascular dementia.
Echopraxia, mitmachen, mutism, staring, and withdrawal directly support catatonia but omit its Lewy body substrate.
Normal TSH makes hypothyroidism an unsupported explanation for the behavioral syndrome.
No asymmetric rigidity, apraxia, alien limb, or cortical sensory sign was observed.
White-matter ischemic changes were labeled chronic and did not match the absence of focal neurologic deficits.
The recorded motor behavior was catatonic, without parkinsonism attributed to antipsychotic exposure.
Late-life visual hallucinations and fluctuating recognition are less consistent with frontotemporal degeneration than the reference subtype.
Chronic MRI white-matter disease was insufficient to explain the subacute hallucinations and classic catatonic signs.

case_quality_flags: Lewy body etiology is incompletely supported because the excerpt reports hallucinations and cognitive fluctuation but no parkinsonism, REM-sleep behavior, or biomarker evaluation.
